title: Streamframe provenance telemetry and redactable trace hooks for progressive outputs
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: We do progressive response delivery (token-by-token / frame-by-frame) for chat and structured outputs. Current telemetry lacks a stable provenance marker for each progressive frame and redaction-aware trace hooks, which makes incident reconstruction and compliance audits error-prone.

Goal: Add a compact, stable 'streamframe' provenance envelope emitted alongside each progressive output frame that enables: deterministic trace stitching across retries/fallbacks, per-frame latency and token-cost attribution, and redactable PII anchors for logs and traces. Provide a small API (runtime + agent SDK) that allows downstream consumers (console, billing, SLO dashboards) to consume per-frame metrics and to request privacy-preserving scrubbed payloads.

Non-goals: This task does not change model sampling or alter tokenization; it does not implement full KV-cache-level instrumentation (that is follow-up).

Deliverables: 1) protobuf-like envelope spec for streamframes, 2) runtime emission points and efficient wire format (binary header + JSON payload option), 3) tracer hook that produces redactable spans with provenance anchors, 4) console dashboard ingest + sample queries, 5) migration path for older clients and compatibility layer for legacy streaming protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Each progressive output frame contains a stable streamframe_id and monotonic sequence index visible in traces and metrics
Latency and token usage per streamframe are exported to telemetry backend with <1ms overhead added to token emission hot path
Trace spans created for streamframes include a redactable_payload_ref that points to a scrubbed/log-safe copy in object store
Runtime can fall back to legacy streaming without breaking clients (compatibility header negotiated at handshake)
E2E tests demonstrating trace stitching across an induced mid-stream failover and model fallback
implementation_notes: Emit a 12-byte binary prefix for low-latency clients: 8B streamframe_id (opaque), 4B sequence uint32
Expose SDK helper to bind a redactable_payload_ref -> object-store blob with HMAC and TTL
Instrumentation should reuse existing metrics buckets (per-request, per-model) and add per-frame histogram tag 'frame_seq'
Avoid JSON allocation on hot path; provide thin C/Go/Node bindings that surface envelope to user-space consumers
Negotiation: extend existing streaming handshake with header 'RW-Streamframe: v1'
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind account-level flag. Stage rollout: dev cluster -> canary (5% traffic) -> regional ramp (25% -> 75%) -> global. During canary verify SLOs and check sampling dashboards. Provide emergency kill switch that strips streamframe envelope at ingress if latency regressions observed.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope encoding/decoding across supported SDKs
Load test simulating 10k concurrent streams to measure overhead
Chaos test: kill worker mid-stream and verify trace stitching and metrics continuity
Privacy test: verify redactable_payload_ref cannot be dereferenced without proper auth and HMAC
logs_and_redaction_policy: Logs must never contain raw progressive output tokens. The runtime will emit only redactable_payload_ref identifiers into logs and traces. A separate scrubber service (configurable per-tenant) will store a scrubbed plaintext blob and record redaction metadata (fields removed, reason). Audit trail: store redaction summary + HMAC of original for forensic-only review under approved compliance flows.
trace_contract: Each streamframe produces a short-lived span with name 'streamframe.emit' and tags: streamframe_id, seq, model, route, tenant_id (hashed). Span contains an attribute 'redactable_payload_ref' referencing the scrubbed blob. Tracers must preserve parent request span id to allow full request -> frames hierarchy.
backward_compatibility: If handshake lacks RW-Streamframe header, runtime omits per-frame envelope and emits legacy stream tokens. Console and billing will map legacy tokens to aggregate metrics only. Provide migration script to reingest sampled legacy streams via stored logs for two-week window.
outstanding_risks: Potential latency regression if envelope emission path is not optimized — mitigated via binary prefix and SDK zero-copy bindings
Storage costs for scrubbed blobs at high QPS — mitigated via TTL and sampling policy
Privacy compliance complexity across regions — need legal sign-off on redactable object retention
Client adoption: older SDKs may ignore new headers leading to partial observability
updates: 2026-03-04: Proto draft v0.1 posted to design doc; initial feedback from SRE requesting smaller envelope footprint
2026-03-06: Spike implemented in Go runtime; microbenchmark shows +0.6% p50 latency, need further optimization
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff scheduled with Compliance (ticket COMP-2201); identified requirement for HMAC-based dereference
2026-03-11: Console engineering prototyped dashboard widgets to surface per-frame latency; storage schema proposed
2026-03-14: Engineering review: approved binary prefix + JSON fallback; assigned SDK owners for C/Go/Node bindings
